title: The torsion diagonal classes as one morphism of inverse systems
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $Y$. Put $W=\mathbf P^1_Y\times_Y\mathbf P^1_Y$ and let
$\Delta:\mathbf P^1_Y\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal, and write $\Delta_*$ for the direct image on pro-etale sheaves from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. After pullback to the pro-etale site, $\mathbf G_m$ denotes $\nu_W^*\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$, where $\mathbf G_{m,W,\mathrm{et}}$ is the etale sheaf of units from [sk-def-kummer], and $\nu_W^*$ is the exact inverse image under the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Use the small site and coefficient-category conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the unbounded derived category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write
$D(W^{\mathbf N}_{\mathrm{proét}})$ for the derived category of inverse systems
$(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ [def-weil-inverse-system] of sheaves of $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-modules on
$W_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Then:

1. The pro-étale pullback of the Cartier extension
   $0\to\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_\Delta\to\Delta_*\mathbf Z\to0$ of the diagonal
   (with $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$ for a local equation $t$ of $\Delta$) defines a
   morphism $\partial:\Delta_*\mathbf Z\to\mathbf G_m[1]$ in
   $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathbf Z)$, represented by the roof
   $\Delta_*\mathbf Z\xleftarrow{\sim}[\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_\Delta]\to\mathbf G_m[1]$
   with the two-term complex in degrees $-1,0$.
2. The functor
   $T:K\mapsto K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}(\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n})_{n\geq1}$
   (the left derived change of rings of the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]) is a well-defined exact functor
   $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathbf Z)\to D(W^{\mathbf N}_{\mathrm{proét}})$, and
   $R\varprojlim\circ T$ is derived $\ell$-completion.
3. There are isomorphisms of systems
   $T(\Delta_*\mathbf Z)\simeq\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet$ and
   $T(\mathbf G_m[1])\simeq\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)[2]$, where the transition
   maps of $\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)=(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf, sk-def-sp-tate-twist] are
   $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$.
4. Under these identifications $c_\bullet=T(\partial)$ is a morphism
   $\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet\to\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)[2]$ in
   $D(W^{\mathbf N}_{\mathrm{proét}})$ whose $n$-th level is the torsion cycle
   class of $\Delta$ with coefficients $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ of
   [sk-lem-geo-cartier].

proof.text: Use the source's standing convention that $\ell$ is prime and invertible on $Y$; $\mathbf G_m$ in the integral extension denotes the pullback $\nu_W^*\mathbf G_{m,\mathrm{et}}$. It need not be identified with the sheaf of all units on every weakly etale object. The first projection W to the projective line is smooth of relative dimension one, by base change of the smooth projective-line projection. The diagonal is a closed immersion and its composite with this projection is the identity. Its kernel subscheme is canonically isomorphic to the diagonal by the universal property of closed immersions with the same ideal. The projection of that subscheme is therefore an isomorphism, hence finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply the already proved Cartier criterion [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] to obtain the invertible diagonal ideal over an arbitrary base, including the empty scheme. In particular the diagonal has regular local equations and its open complement is quasi-compact over W, being a principal open locally on W. On an etale chart with local equation $t$, define $\mathcal M_\Delta$ as the subgroup of the units on the complement locally generated by units and all integral powers of $t^{-1}$. Replacing $t$ by $vt$ with $v$ a unit preserves this subgroup. For an affine etale neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of such a chart, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] makes $B$ flat over $A$: tensoring the injection $A\xrightarrow{t}A$ proves that $t$ remains regular on that neighbourhood. Exactness of geometric stalks then keeps multiplication by $t$ injective in the stalk. At a geometric stalk on $\Delta$, $t$ is also a nonunit. If $ut^{-a}=vt^{-b}$ and $a>b$, injectivity of localization at the regular element $t$ gives $u=vt^{a-b}$, making $t$ a unit, a contradiction; interchanging the two expressions excludes $b>a$. Thus $a=b$, and conversely every integer is the pole order of $t^{-a}$. Off $\Delta$ this quotient is zero. The closed immersion $\Delta$ is finite: locally it is given by the cyclic finite algebra $A\to A/(t)$. The finite direct-image stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] gives one factor $\mathbf Z$ on the diagonal fibre and the zero product off the diagonal, identifying exactly the quotient stalks just computed. Thus the stalk sequences are exact, and [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] give $0\to\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_\Delta\to\Delta_*\mathbf Z\to0$ on the etale site, with $t^{-1}\mapsto1$. There is no bound of one on the pole order: sections with at most a simple pole would not be closed under multiplication.

source.place: Proof (1), local construction and correction of “at most a simple pole”

proof.text:
The site comparison of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and the general inverse-image theorem [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] make $
u_W^*$ exact on abelian sheaves and identify pulled constant $\mathbf Z$ with constant $\mathbf Z$. The closed supported constant comparison can be verified without a coefficient finiteness assumption. Put $N=
u_W^*(\Delta_*^{\mathrm{et}}\mathbf Z)$. It vanishes on the open complement. Inverse image along $\Delta$ commutes with $
u^*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and the restriction of the etale supported constant is $\mathbf Z$ (check its geometric stalks, using the stalk exactness and conservativity from step 1). Thus $\Delta^{-1}N=\mathbf Z$. The open--closed exact sequence in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied with ring $\mathbf Z$ and $j^{-1}N=0$, makes its unit $N	o\Delta_*\mathbf Z$ an isomorphism. Apply exact $
u_W^*$ to the extension of step 1 with this comparison. The quotient map $[\mathbf G_m	o\mathcal M_\Delta]	o\Delta_*\mathbf Z$ is now a quasi-isomorphism: its cohomology in degree $-1$ is zero and in degree $0$ is the quotient. Projection onto degree $-1$ is a chain map to $\mathbf G_m[1]$. Localizing this roof gives the specified boundary $\partial$, with the extension sign fixed by $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$.

source.place: Proof (1), exact pullback, supported comparison and roof

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell})$ on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ in a fixed small universe. [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] supplies all small colimits of $\mathcal A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-functor-abelian-colimits] makes $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal A)$ abelian. Kernels and cokernels are formed componentwise: the transition on a kernel is induced by the commuting square, and on a cokernel by its quotient property; these constructions satisfy the kernel and cokernel universal properties componentwise. Hence evaluation is exact and cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms are detected at all levels. Define on homotopy complexes $F(P)=(P\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n})_n$, and then localize its output in $D(\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal A))$, with quotient transitions and the $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ action through $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. Tensor commutes with shifts and maps the mapping cone of a chain map to the mapping cone of its tensor map, term by term, so $F$ is triangulated. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] every input has a flat-term K-flat resolution. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] $F$ takes a quasi-isomorphism between such resolutions to a quasi-isomorphism at every level, hence in this actual system category. The resolving-class theorem [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] therefore constructs an everywhere-defined exact functor $T=LF$ computed by one such resolution; it acts on morphisms and supplies canonical resolution comparisons in the system category. This proves clause (2)'s functoriality, rather than assembling independently chosen derived level maps.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YY; resolving-class descent and elementary componentwise kernel/cokernel calculation

proof.text: First compare the two coefficient categories in the inverse limit. The ring $\mathbf Z_\ell=\varprojlim_r\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ is torsion free over $\mathbf Z$: multiplication by an integer prime to $\ell$ is invertible on each quotient; if $\ell a=0$, the coordinate of $a$ modulo $\ell^{r+1}$ is divisible by $\ell^r$, so its coordinate modulo $\ell^r$ vanishes for every $r$. Factor any nonzero integer as a power of $\ell$ times an integer prime to $\ell$. Since $\mathbf Z$ is a principal ideal domain, [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] gives flatness of $\mathbf Z_\ell$ over $\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-flat] with coefficient category $\operatorname{Ab}$, flat object $\mathbf Z_\ell$, and terminal site object $W$: there is exactly one arrow $V\to W$, so its free presheaf is the constant $\mathbf Z_\ell$ presheaf. Thus tensor with $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ is exact on integral sheaves. The module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], for the identity topos and $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$, is therefore an exact extension of scalars left adjoint to restriction. Apply it componentwise to strict systems; the adjunction and exactness are componentwise as in step 3. The strict module-system category is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck], with small index $J$, so [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] supplies K-injective resolutions. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], restriction sends a K-injective system complex to an integral K-injective system complex. Ordinary restriction commutes with inverse limits: both underlying sheaves are the sheaf of compatible tuples, with the scalar action forgotten. Therefore deriving inverse limit with this same resolution gives a natural isomorphism between restriction of $R\varprojlim$ in $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module systems and integral $R\varprojlim$ of the restricted system. Now the underlying integral composite $R\varprojlim\circ T$ is $R\varprojlim_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n})$ with the strict quotient transitions of step 3. Apply [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] with the small site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, Noetherian ring $A=\mathbf Z$ and ideal $I=(\ell)$. Its completion formula identifies exactly this functor with derived $\ell$-completion. The original composite retains its constant-$\mathbf Z_\ell$ action. All comparisons used an actual K-injective resolution of a strict system, not an arbitrary choice of a cone in a triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion; scalar-restriction comparison by exact scalar adjunction and K-injective resolutions (agent expansion)

proof.text: Put $i=\Delta$ and let $j$ be the complement. For a $\mathbf Z$-module sheaf $H$ consider the natural map $(i_*\mathbf Z)\otimes H\to i_*i^{-1}H$, adjoint to the tensor evaluation after $i^{-1}$. Its open restriction is the isomorphism $0\to0$, and its closed restriction is $\mathbf Z\otimes i^{-1}H\to i^{-1}H$, the usual multiplication isomorphism. Here inverse image is exact and monoidal by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives $i^{-1}i_*=1$, $j^{-1}i_*=0$ and the open--closed sequence. Applying that sequence to the kernel and cokernel of the displayed map proves they vanish. Since $i^{-1}$ and $i_*$ are exact, $H\mapsto i_*i^{-1}H$ is exact, so $i_*\mathbf Z$ is flat. To compute its reduction, the two-term free resolution $[\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf Z]$ of $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ is K-flat: tensoring it with an acyclic complex is the cone of multiplication by $\ell^n$ on that complex, hence is acyclic. Its tensor with $i_*\mathbf Z$ has zero kernel and cokernel $i_*\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, because $i_*$ is exact. These identifications are natural under the quotient maps at all levels; alternatively the flat object itself computes all its tensors at once. This yields the source-system identification of clause (3).

source.place: Proof (3), Source; explicit open/closed tensor calculation (Tag 09AD)

proof.text: At level $n$ apply [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] to $m=\ell^n$ on the etale site; invertibility is exactly the standing hypothesis. Pull its short exact Kummer sequence to the pro-etale site by the exact inverse image in [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. The pulled root sheaf is the actual finite root sheaf: apply [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](1) with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $r=n$ to obtain an etale root-trivializing cover. On this cover a chosen primitive root defines the generator of the etale roots sheaf and of the actual pro-etale roots sheaf. Exact inverse image preserves the constant finite cyclic sheaf, and the roots comparison sends that generator to the identical root, hence is an isomorphism there and therefore globally. Write $Q_n=[\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf Z]$ in degrees $-1,0$, the K-flat resolution from step 5. To justify computing in the second factor, take the K-flat resolution $P\to\mathbf G_m$ supplied in step 3. The two maps $P\otimes Q_n\to P\otimes\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n}$ and $P\otimes Q_n\to\mathbf G_m\otimes Q_n$ are quasi-isomorphisms: their cones are obtained by tensoring the acyclic cones of $Q_n\to\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n}$ and $P\to\mathbf G_m$ with the K-flat complexes $P$ and $Q_n$, respectively, as in [def-pc-kflat-complex]. These maps commute with every transition $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. Thus, as integral complexes, the underlying derived tensors and their transitions are computed by $[\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf G_m]$ in degrees $-1,0$. Kummer exactness gives its only cohomology $\mu_{\ell^n}$ in degree $-1$. The reduction of resolutions from $n+1$ to $n$ is multiplication by $\ell$ in degree $-1$ and the identity in degree $0$: $\ell^n\ell=\ell^{n+1}$. Thus it induces $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$ on that kernel, the transition specified in [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Fix the sign of the target identification as follows. In additive notation put $B=\mathbf G_m$, $H=\mu_{\ell^n}$, $m=\ell^n$ and write $\iota:H\to B$ for the kernel inclusion. Set $E=[H\xrightarrow{\iota}B]$ and $C=[B\xrightarrow{m}B]$, both in degrees $-1,0$. Thus $E$ is the mapping cone of $\iota$, $q=(0,m):E\to B$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $p=(1,0):E\to H[1]$ is the projection. The cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] has third arrow $-p$ (Stacks 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), so the Kummer connecting morphism of $0\to H\to B\xrightarrow{m}B\to0$ used by [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] is $\kappa_B=-p\circ q^{-1}$; step 7 proves that this boundary is unique. Under the common-resolution comparison above, the scalar-extension unit $B\to C$ is inclusion in degree $0$: the degree-zero inclusion $\mathbf Z[0]\to Q_n$ lifts the quotient $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z/m$. Its composite with $q$ has degree-zero component $m$ and degree-minus-one component zero. This map is homotopic to the composite $E\xrightarrow{p}H[1]\xrightarrow{-\iota}C$: the homotopy $h^0:E^0=B\to C^{-1}=B$ is the identity, and $dh+hd$ has components $\iota$ in degree $-1$ and $m$ in degree $0$, which is the difference of the two chain maps. Hence the unit is $(-\iota)\circ p\circ q^{-1}=\iota\circ\kappa_B$, so the normalized identification $\alpha_B$ of the route lemma is the inverse of the positive kernel inclusion $\iota:H[1]\to C$. This item uses instead $\psi=-\alpha_B$, the inverse of $-\iota$, at every level; equivalently $\psi$ sends the unit to the positive roof $p\circ q^{-1}=-\kappa_B$, the same positive-roof convention by which clause (1) fixes $\partial$. This uniform sign commutes with the power transitions just computed. Step 7 shows that the two positive-roof conventions cancel, so clause (4) holds with $\psi$. This computation describes underlying integral complexes. At level $n$ the cohomology action factors through $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, so integer multiples determine it uniquely and the signed root identification is linear. No $\mathbf Z_\ell$-action on $\mathbf G_m$ is presumed. Cohomology of the genuine $\mathbf Z_\ell$-linear system $T(\mathbf G_m[1])$ is therefore concentrated in degree $-2$. For a complex $C$ representing this object, form the good truncation $\tau_{\leq-2}C$ of [def-kun-truncations]. Its map to $C$ induces the identity on the sole nonzero cohomology, hence is a quasi-isomorphism. The quotient map $\ker(d^{-2}_C)\to H^{-2}(C)$ defines a chain map $\tau_{\leq-2}C\to H^{-2}(C)[2]$, zero in all lower degrees; it too induces the identity on the sole cohomology, hence is a quasi-isomorphism. These kernels, quotients and maps are in the system module category, so this roof preserves the scalar action and every transition. Identify $H^{-2}(C)$ with $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$ by the signed identification $\psi$ just fixed. The truncation roof then yields the system isomorphism $T(\mathbf G_m[1])\simeq(\mu_{\ell^n})_n[2]$. The finite twist formula of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] identifies this with $\mathbf Z/\ell^\bullet(1)[2]$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence; explicit two-term-resolution transition calculation

proof.text:
Write $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the Cartier extension constructed in step 1, and $S=\nu_W^*S_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the extension and boundary $\partial$ of step 2. Fix a level $n\geq1$ and put $m=\ell^n$ and $R=\underline{\mathbf Z/m}$. On both sites multiplication by $m$ on $B=\mathbf G_m$ is an epimorphism by the Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] and its exact pullback, while multiplication by $m$ on $F=\Delta_*\mathbf Z$ is a monomorphism by the stalk calculation of step 1 and exact pullback. Thus [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction] applies to these exact sequences on the small sites with final object $W$. Its identifications are $\alpha_F:Lq(F)\simeq F/mF=\Delta_*R$ and $\alpha_B:Lq(B)\simeq\mu_m[1]$, the latter normalized so that the scalar-extension unit is the Kummer connecting morphism $\kappa_B$. It defines $d_{S,m}=\alpha_B[1]\circ Lq(\partial_S)\circ\alpha_F^{-1}$ as an actual morphism of $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$, where $\partial_S$ is the last arrow of the derived short-exact-sequence triangle [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]; this is a reduction of the full supported morphism, not a characterization by its composite with $R_W\to\Delta_*R$. Compare $\partial_S$ with the statement's $\partial$. For $a:\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_\Delta$ and the quotient $g$, the two-term complex $[\mathbf G_m\to\mathcal M_\Delta]$ is the mapping cone of $a$; let $q$ be its quasi-isomorphism to $\Delta_*\mathbf Z$ and $p$ its projection to $\mathbf G_m[1]$. The cone-triangle convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $(\mathbf G_m,\mathcal M_\Delta,\Delta_*\mathbf Z,a,g,-p\circ q^{-1})$ distinguished (Stacks 0152). If $\delta'$ also completes $a,g$ to a distinguished triangle, TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] applied with identities on $\mathbf G_m$ and $\mathcal M_\Delta$ gives $c:\Delta_*\mathbf Z\to\Delta_*\mathbf Z$ with $cg=g$ and $-p\circ q^{-1}=\delta'c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], $c$ is a sheaf endomorphism, and $g$ is an epimorphism, so $c=\mathrm{id}$. Hence $\partial_S=-p\circ q^{-1}=-\partial$, because clause (1) defines $\partial$ by the positive roof $p\circ q^{-1}$. The same argument for the Kummer sequence proves $\kappa_B=-p\circ q^{-1}$, as used in step 6. With $\psi=-\alpha_B$ from step 6,
$$\psi[1]\circ Lq(\partial)\circ\alpha_F^{-1}=(-\alpha_B[1])\circ(-Lq(\partial_S))\circ\alpha_F^{-1}=d_{S,m}.$$
The two sign conventions cancel.

To compare with the torsion cycle class specified in clause (4), use its defining construction in the source sk-lem-geo-cartier.proof.md, the paragraph beginning “The boundary of (G1)”: for $\Lambda=R$ it applies derived reduction to the boundary of the meromorphic Cartier extension, with $t^{-1}\mapsto+1$, then applies $\nu_W^*$. This is exactly $d_{S_{\mathrm{et}},m}$ on the etale site. The naturality under exact inverse image in [lem-sfb-divisible-extension-derived-reduction], together with the derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], gives $\nu_W^*d_{S_{\mathrm{et}},m}=d_{S,m}$, using the supported-constant identification of step 2 and the roots identification of step 6. These source identifications are the canonical units/counits of closed restriction: on the closed support their counits are the identity and off it both sides vanish, so the open--closed sequence gives their unique inverse. For the target, step 6 shows that the lemma's $\alpha_B$ is the inverse of the positive kernel inclusion $\iota:\mu_m[1]\to[\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{m}\mathbf G_m]$, and that this item's identification is $\psi=-\alpha_B$. By the display above, $\psi$ together with the positive roof $\partial$ gives $d_{S,m}$. Both the lemma's naturality and the exact inverse image preserve this uniform sign. The identifications agree as finite $R$-linear identifications: after the common K-flat comparison they induce the same signed map on the sole cohomology sheaf, which determines a morphism between objects concentrated in that one cohomological degree.

Evaluation of the single K-flat construction in step 3, keeping its $R$ action, is the same functor $Lq$: on a K-flat resolution $P$ both are $P\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R$, on morphisms both tensor the same resolution maps, and the canonical comparison of resolutions is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Therefore its level-$n$ morphism, read through $\alpha_F$ and $\psi$, is $\psi[1]\circ Lq(\partial)\circ\alpha_F^{-1}=d_{S,m}$ in $D(R)$, and after restriction along $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}\to R$ it is that same morphism in the evaluated category. With the system identifications of steps 5--6, $c_\bullet=T(\partial)$ thus has the required finite Cartier cycle class at every level. Compatibility between levels is already furnished by the single system functor $T$ and its quotient transitions; it is not inferred from equality of separately chosen level maps, nor from the first-Chern composite equation in [sk-lem-geo-cartier].

Compared evaluation of T with finite-ring derived reduction on a common K-flat resolution and identified the cycle class by its source definition, without inferring equality from the first-Chern composite equation. Added the finite direct-image stalk formula to step 1, removed the unsupported relative-torsor route, pruned obsolete dependencies and replaced boilerplate tool-use reasons. No new nodes. Second reading expanded pole-order uniqueness and the two-factor K-flat comparison, instantiated the root-trivializing lemma and replaced the ambiguous Cartier source paragraph number by its opening words. Corrected the target-system sign by an explicit chain homotopy so that the scalar-extension unit is the Kummer connecting map, as required by the Cartier route lemma. Q121 resumed the existing corrected proof unchanged, verified its citations and source, restored status split, and completed the unit realization map using the four existing diagonal-tower nodes.
